use: Only for people, never things; often oozei no hito.

example.romaji: kinou, oozei kite taihen datta.
example.ja: 昨日、大勢来て大変だった。
example.english: Tons of people came yesterday, it was crazy.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou wa oozei kite taihen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日は大勢来て大変でした。
examplePolite.english: Lots of people came yesterday, so it was hectic.

notes: Mix-up: takusan works for anything; oozei is people only.

use: Rough and often insulting; also used to call an adult childish.

example.romaji: omae, mada gaki da na.
example.ja: お前、まだガキだな。
example.english: You're still such a kid.

use: Said about people who report to you, never to address them.

example.romaji: buka ga yamechatta n da.
example.ja: 部下が辞めちゃったんだ。
example.english: One of my team quit.

examplePolite.romaji: buka ga yamete shimatta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 部下が辞めてしまったんです。

english: member (of a team, band or group)
use: Also the lineup of people at an event: kyou no menbaa.

example.romaji: kyou no menbaa, dare?
example.ja: 今日のメンバー、誰？
example.english: Who's coming today?

examplePolite.romaji: kyou no menbaa wa dare desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今日のメンバーは誰ですか？

use: Mostly as uwaki suru (to cheat) and uwaki sareta (got cheated on).

example.romaji: kare ni uwaki sareta.
example.ja: 彼に浮気された。
example.english: My boyfriend cheated on me.

notes: For an affair involving a married person, furin is more common.

use: School students, especially junior high and high school; also someone taking lessons.

example.romaji: ano sensei, seito ni ninki aru yo.
example.ja: あの先生、生徒に人気あるよ。
example.english: That teacher is popular with the students.

examplePolite.romaji: ano sensei wa seito ni ninki ga arimasu.
examplePolite.ja: あの先生は生徒に人気があります。
examplePolite.english: That teacher is popular with the students.

use: Someone who joined after you; they call you senpai.

example.romaji: kore, kouhai ni moratta n da.
example.ja: これ、後輩にもらったんだ。
example.english: I got this from one of my juniors.

examplePolite.ja: これは後輩にもらいました。
examplePolite.english: One of my juniors gave me this.

notes: Opposite: senpai. Who joined first decides it, not age.

use: The everyday neutral word; josei is more formal, onna can sound blunt.

example.romaji: ano onna no hito, shitteru?
example.ja: あの女の人、知ってる？
example.english: Do you know that woman?

examplePolite.romaji: ano onna no hito o shitte imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの女の人を知っていますか？

example.romaji: musuko, mada shougakusei na n da.
example.ja: 息子、まだ小学生なんだ。
example.english: My son's still in elementary school.

examplePolite.ja: 息子はまだ小学生です。
examplePolite.english: My son is still in elementary school.

use: Also a group chat or a pop group.

example.romaji: guruupu ni shashin okuttoku ne.
example.ja: グループに写真送っとくね。
example.english: I'll send the photos to the group.

examplePolite.romaji: guruupu ni shashin o okutte okimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: グループに写真を送っておきますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll send the photos to the group.

use: Used loosely as praise, even for small things.

example.romaji: e, mou dekita no? tensai ja nai?
example.ja: え、もうできたの？天才じゃない？
example.english: Wait, done already? You're a genius!

examplePolite.romaji: mou dekita n desu ka? tensai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: もうできたんですか？天才ですね。

notes: Mix-up: tensai also means natural disaster (天災).

english: classmate; someone in your year at school
use: Same year at school, even if not the same class.

example.romaji: kare, koukou no doukyuusei na n da.
example.ja: 彼、高校の同級生なんだ。
example.english: He was in my year in high school.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa koukou no doukyuusei desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は高校の同級生です。
examplePolite.english: We were in the same year in high school.

notes: kurasumeito means the same class only.

example.romaji: kore, koukousei no toki no shashin.
example.ja: これ、高校生の時の写真。
example.english: This is me in high school.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa koukousei no toki no shashin desu.
examplePolite.ja: これは高校生の時の写真です。
examplePolite.english: This is a photo from when I was in high school.

example.romaji: akachan neteru kara, shizuka ni ne.
example.ja: 赤ちゃん寝てるから、静かにね。
example.english: The baby's asleep, so keep it down.

examplePolite.romaji: akachan ga nete iru node, shizuka ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 赤ちゃんが寝ているので、静かにしてください。
examplePolite.english: The baby is sleeping, so please be quiet.

notes: Also for baby animals: neko no akachan (a kitten).

use: A really close friend; you can have more than one.

example.romaji: kanojo wa shougakkou kara no shin'yuu na n da.
example.ja: 彼女は小学校からの親友なんだ。
example.english: She's been my best friend since elementary school.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa shougakkou kara no shin'yuu desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女は小学校からの親友です。
examplePolite.english: She's been my best friend since elementary school.

use: Young people as a group, often said by older people or the media.

example.romaji: saikin no wakamono wa terebi minai yo ne.
example.ja: 最近の若者はテレビ見ないよね。
example.english: Young people these days don't watch TV, right?

examplePolite.romaji: saikin no wakamono wa terebi o mimasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 最近の若者はテレビを見ませんね。
examplePolite.english: Young people these days don't watch TV.

notes: wakai hito is the softer everyday way to say it.

use: People at your level at work.

example.romaji: kinou, douryou to nomi ni itta.
example.ja: 昨日、同僚と飲みに行った。
example.english: I went drinking with coworkers yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, douryou to nomi ni ikimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、同僚と飲みに行きました。
examplePolite.english: I went for drinks with coworkers yesterday.

notes: In chat people often just say kaisha no hito.

use: Used when at least one person is married; often furin suru.

example.romaji: ano futari, furin shiteru rashii yo.
example.ja: あの二人、不倫してるらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently those two are having an affair.

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari wa furin shite iru rashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は不倫しているらしいです。
examplePolite.english: I hear those two are having an affair.

notes: Mix-up: uwaki is cheating in general, including while dating.

use: Someone who isn't a professional or doesn't know the field.

example.romaji: shirouto da kara, yoku wakannai yo.
example.ja: 素人だから、よくわかんないよ。
example.english: I'm no expert, so I don't really get it.

examplePolite.ja: 素人なので、よくわかりません。
examplePolite.english: I'm not an expert, so I don't really understand.

use: Used like a name to address the manager at shops and restaurants.

example.romaji: tenchou ni kiite kuru ne.
example.ja: 店長に聞いてくるね。
example.english: I'll go ask the manager.

examplePolite.english: I'll go and ask the manager.
